title: Neural heart measurements reveal a chest-pain risk association
summary: Two U-Net models measured heart volume in CT scans from 3,798 PROMISE participants. Smaller body-size-indexed volume was associated with subsequent major adverse events, particularly in patients with non-obstructive coronary disease. This retrospective secondary analysis is hypothesis-generating; it does not establish a causal mechanism, a normal-volume threshold or improved clinical decisions.
organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School; Duke University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Automated CT measurements linked to independently adjudicated events over median 26-month follow-up in a randomized-trial cohort.
evidence.unknown: Independent prognostic validation and clinical utility remain unestablished; patients with known coronary disease or heart failure were excluded and subgroup event counts were limited.
evidence.ai_role: Two pretrained U-Nets localize and segment the heart, enabling standardized volumetric measurements for clinical event-association analysis.
